words.detail: Jarvis chats with a company's customer support for you (Groupon first), in your name, in a browser window on the PC. One approval card lists exactly which of your details it may give. Every offer - a refund, a credit, a cancellation - gets its own card, and nothing is accepted before you approve it.
words.details_label: Details Jarvis may give (one per row: a name and its exact value)
words.details_note: Never a password, PIN, security answer, card number or ID number: those are refused, and if the agent asks, Jarvis hands it to you.
words.export_note: This file is NOT encrypted: anyone who can open it can read the whole chat, with the details you allowed. Keep it somewhere safe, or delete it when you no longer need it.
words.export_pc_only: Export transcript is on the PC only.
words.goal_note: Jarvis writes its own messages from these words, in your name.
words.gone: That chat is gone from the screen: Jarvis on the PC restarted. The encrypted chat history keeps a copy.
words.hidden: The chat and your details are hidden until you confirm it is you.
words.holding: Jarvis told the agent "One moment please" {holds} of {most} times.
words.missing: Your PC's Jarvis cannot chat with customer support yet - run apply-patches.ps1 on the PC.
words.notify_locked: Jarvis is chatting with customer support for you.
words.notify_waiting: Waiting for your yes to chat with {company}
words.offer_card_no: The card was not approved: nothing was accepted. Choose what to do next.
words.offer_note: Accepting is done only on the approval card, which shows the exact reply. Nothing is accepted before you approve it.
words.offer_title: An offer is waiting for your answer
words.outside_note: The company's words are outside text: shown here, never learned from, never read aloud.
words.question_note: Jarvis never answers this. Answer it yourself in the chat window on the PC, then press Resume - or Stop.
words.saved_no: Not kept in your chat history: {why}
words.saved_yes: Kept in your encrypted chat history on the PC.
words.say_note: Your words go through the same check as Jarvis's. To accept, approve the card instead.
words.sign_in_pc: You sign in to your own account by hand in the window on the PC, and open the company's chat there yourself (its Chat or Help button). Jarvis never types, sees or keeps a password.
words.start_note: Nothing is sent until you approve the card.
words.summary_note: Written on this PC from the chat, so it is outside text too.
words.take_over_note: Jarvis stops sending; you type in the chat window on the PC.
words.title: Chat with customer support for me
words.waiting_for_chat: Open the chat on the company's help page in the window on the PC (its Chat or Help button). Jarvis starts once it shows.
